messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: Sev2 - Customer 'AtlasCorp' (enterprise VPC atlas-vpc-01) reporting websocket stream resets and gateway 502/504s. Symptoms: repeated reconnect loops, elevated error rates, potential cross-tenant latency increases. Paging #oncall. Incident ref INC-1937.

sam: acked. Oncall here. Kicking off triage. Maria, can you pull the last 15m of ws connection events, and check for deploys to atlas-vpc-01? Also tag eng-runtime.

maria: looking. No deploys in the last hour. At ~02:02 UTC we see a spike of aborted websockets from atlas gateway: client FIN after ~20-35s, then gateway retries open new ws within 2-6s. Our edge returns 502 or 504 depending on handshake state. CPU and event-loop backlog on pool nodes increased ~3x during the spike.

neil: initial theory: their gateway idle/timeout or health probe is closing sockets; their retry policy is very tight causing connection re-creation storms. Because atlas-vpc-01 is currently packed, this behavior is producing noisy-tenant effects.

sam: quick mitigation plan options?

jess: propose immediate mitigations, in order: 1) apply tenant-level circuit-breaker for new websocket opens (reject if opens/sec > 5 with 429), 2) set tenant edge retry_policy to 0 to avoid duplicate backends, 3) enable early-ack proxy mode for streams so we don't hold backend connection for full idle time, 4) move atlas to isolated failover pool atlas-vpc-isolated if config change not confirmed. I can prepare CLI steps.

maria: telemetry suggests the reconnect_rate for atlascorp peaked at 12/s. Co-tenant p95 token latency rose from 280ms -> 1.2s. Agree with jess ordering.

sam: apply steps 1-2 now. I'll coordinate with CSM to get the customer to adjust their gateway retry/timeout settings.

[~execution by sam]

```
# redwoodctl
redwoodctl tenants patch atlascorp --edge-controls '{"ws_open_rate_limit":5,"retry_policy":{"max_retries":0}}'
```

incident-bot: ACTION: edge_controls applied by sam at 1937001320. ws_open_rate_limit=5, retry_policy.max_retries=0. Monitoring for 10m.

maria: immediate effect: new ws open attempts throttled from 12/s -> 4/s, CPU/backlog dipped ~45% in 90s. Error volume to customer reduced but they still report occasional client-facing 502s.

neil: next step: buffered proxy (early-ack) will reduce backend hold-time further. Jess, can you enable it for atlascorp as a temporary flag? It's safe to switch—will alter streaming semantics slightly (chunked ack).

jess: enabling buffered-proxy mode now and adding temporary rate limiter on per-connection token generation to limit backend pressure. Command below.

```
redwoodctl tenants patch atlascorp --streaming-mode buffered-proxy --token-rate-limit 120/s
```

incident-bot: ACTION: buffered-proxy enabled by jess at 1937001385. token-rate-limit=120/s.

maria: after buffered-proxy, backend connection hold-time reduced by ~70%. Co-tenant latencies returned near baseline. Client-reported session continuity improved but atlas gateway still shows sporadic 502s when their gateway gives up quickly.

anna (CSM): I've reached out to AtlasCorp. They provided their gateway config: idle_timeout=30s, retry_interval=3s, max_retries=5. They're testing a change to set idle_timeout=120s and disable aggressive retries in staging now. They've asked us to confirm whether buffered-proxy has any side effects for their app (we documented expected behavior and they acknowledged).

neil: long-term mitigation suggestions: (A) offer single-tenant fully isolated pool for atlas streaming SLA, (B) default dedicated pool packing policy for streaming tenants should avoid co-tenants, (C) implement automatic detect-and-quarantine for tenants that exceed reconnect_rate threshold, (D) server-side keepalive handshake/heartbeat to survive intermediate gateway timeouts.

jess: agree. I'll draft a follow-up plan: immediate deliverables: runbook update (add ws_open_rate_limit and buffered-proxy steps), telemetry: reconnect_rate and gateway-FIN detection, and product: review dedicated pool packing. Also propose a feature: "edge backpressure signal" to surface to customer gateway—HTTP header or 429 with Retry-After to let them back off gracefully.

sam: incident status: mitigated by edge limits + buffered proxy; customer engaged and testing config change. Severity remains Sev2 pending 2h stable or customer confirmation. Handoff to jess for 4h watch. Postmortem owner: jess. Customer comms: anna (CSM).

platform-bot: INC-1937 created. Notifying #enterprise and #product. Auto-reminder in 60m to update thread and escalate if unstable.

maria: exporting logs/traces for postmortem: ws-open sequence with FIN timestamps, throttled opens, and backend token-rate stats. Will attach to incident doc.

jess: I'll open a dedicated PR for runbook and add an RFC for default packing policy for streaming tenants. Also will propose a new alert: tenant_reconnect_rate > 5/s for 1m triggers auto-rate-limit action.

sam: good work. Quick cross-team action: eng-runtime to prototype a fast path that rejects immediate reconnects from same client IP for N seconds to avoid amplification loops. Also CS to confirm customer will deploy timeout changes to prod.

incident-bot: REMINDER: update incident within 60m. If stable for 30m and Atlas confirms gateway changes in prod, we close as mitigated and begin postmortem.

[thread end]
